rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and visible ICM/zona thinning, but it overstates certainty about TE cohesion, blastocoel fullness, and exact hatching location from this single image; also labels stage 4 as hatching despite herniation being more consistent with stage 5.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve markers, prior failed cycles, BMI, sperm quality, endometrium, protocol choice, and embryo grade into prognosis and planning.

Reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with probability adjustments explained; minor issues include overinterpretation of recurrent implantation failure after only two failed cycles and some speculative protocol conclusions.

Much is evidence-based (SET for a good-quality blastocyst, attention to uterine factors), but several recommendations are not strongly guideline-supported or are controversial, including ERA, immunologic testing/treatments, routine thrombophilia workup, aspirin, intralipids, and broad endorsement of PGT-A in this scenario.

Provides clear next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, and further evaluation if unsuccessful; slightly reduced by inclusion of controversial add-ons without sufficient prioritization.
